entries.thesis: IGV was newly highlighted for observation due to longer relative strength, not a buy call, while short-term five-session performance was negative.
entries.counterevidence: The five-session return was weak and rising discount rates could pressure software sector valuations.
entries.invalidation: Further deterioration in relative strength, credit stress or weak independent earnings evidence would invalidate improvement thesis.
entries.revisit_trigger: Reassess after 5/10/20 US sessions and verify independently reported software earnings and guidance.

entries.thesis: XLY was highlighted as a watch list candidate based on relative strength, with continuation unproven and the prior 63-session return slightly negative.
entries.counterevidence: Fragile market breadth, potentially elevated interest rates and soft 63-session trend reduce confidence in continuation.
entries.invalidation: Fading relative strength, persistently weak real demand or declining earnings and company guidance undermine the watch thesis.
entries.revisit_trigger: Reassess after 5/10/20 US sessions against SPY and independently verify sector earnings and consumer trends.

entries.thesis: IHF was specifically highlighted for closer healthcare providers and insurers observation, distinct from a new automated candidate entry or buy signal.
entries.counterevidence: Insurance cost ratios, reimbursement/regulatory sensitivity, narrower exposure than XLV and weaker than expected volume confirmation.
entries.invalidation: Deteriorating SPY relative strength, adverse insurance policy/claims outcomes, issuer results or liquidity deterioration.
entries.revisit_trigger: Reassess after 5/10/20 US sessions and independently review health-insurer regulatory and earnings updates.

entries.thesis: The report began closer observation of XLV on relative strength and a price above its 50-session average, without proposing a purchase.
entries.counterevidence: A prior price rally may already be reflected, while pharmaceutical, insurance and equipment fundamentals and regulation differ.
entries.invalidation: Persistent deterioration relative to SPY, a renewed break below the 50-session average, or worsening major company earnings.
entries.revisit_trigger: Reassess 5/10/20 US sessions later with sector-wide results, ETF structure and valuation.

entries.thesis: No newly validated ETF purchase candidate or allocation change; retain existing observations and do not treat one-day SOXX rebound as trend reversal.
entries.counterevidence: Lam Research sales and Meta data-center capital expenditure increased, but do not establish broad SOXX constituent demand.
entries.invalidation: Reassess if multiple suppliers' orders, shipments, cash flow, rates, ETF relative strength and issuer information are independently verified.
entries.revisit_trigger: Revisit market stance after 5, 10 and 20 NYSE trading sessions using SPY as context; no ticker-specific return attribution for this MARKET entry.

entries.thesis: No new verified ETF buy candidate or account allocation change in the Oct 23 public research report because the latest health gate was ERROR and issuer, fund structure, valuation and liquidity evidence did not support a new entry.
entries.counterevidence: XLV and IHF exhibited relative strength, XLP and XLU had defensive momentum, chip equipment and analog company revenues grew, and a substantial share of S&P 500 constituents rose despite index weakness.
entries.invalidation: Reconsider the no-new-candidate stance when the judgment-ledger health error is revalidated as resolved and independent ETF fund characteristics, relative strength, company orders, cash flow and macro/credit evidence support a clearly better opportunity.
entries.revisit_trigger: Review the overall opportunity set after 5, 10 and 20 NYSE sessions without attributing ticker-specific predictive hit rates to a MARKET no-new-candidate entry.
